headline.text: EU countries must apply the pay transparency rules by 7 June 2026, and the first gender pay gap reports are due by 7 June 2027.

what_changed.text: Employers must give job applicants the starting pay or its range and may not ask about their pay history.
Employers with 150 or more workers report their gender pay gap from 7 June 2027; those with 100 to 149 from 7 June 2031.

who.text: French and Spanish employers of every size in hospitality, retail and construction are covered; those with 100 to 249 workers also report pay gaps.

money.text: The text sets no fine amount; Member States set fines under national law, and compensation for pay discrimination has no upper limit.

facts.statement: EU countries must bring their pay transparency laws into force by 7 June 2026.

citation.quote: Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 7 June 2026.

facts.statement: The directive covers employers in both the public and the private sector.

citation.quote: This Directive applies to employers in public and private sectors.

facts.statement: Employers must tell job applicants the starting pay or its range for the position, based on gender-neutral criteria.

citation.quote: the initial pay or its range, based on objective, gender-neutral criteria, to be attributed for the position concerned; and

facts.statement: Employers can give this pay information in the published job ad, before the interview, or by other means.

citation.quote: Such information shall be provided in a manner such as to ensure an informed and transparent negotiation on pay, such as in a published job vacancy notice, prior to the job interview or otherwise.

facts.statement: Employers may not ask applicants about their pay in current or previous jobs.

citation.quote: An employer shall not ask applicants about their pay history during their current or previous employment relationships.

facts.statement: Employers must give workers easy access to the criteria that set pay, pay levels and pay progression.

citation.quote: Employers shall make easily accessible to their workers the criteria that are used to determine workers’ pay, pay levels and pay progression.

facts.statement: Member States can exempt employers with fewer than 50 workers from the pay progression criteria duty.

citation.quote: Member States may exempt employers with fewer than 50 workers from the obligation related to the pay progression set out in paragraph 1.

facts.statement: Workers can request in writing their own pay level and the average pay by sex for workers doing equal work.

citation.quote: Workers shall have the right to request and receive in writing, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 4, information on their individual pay level and the average pay levels, broken down by sex, for categories of workers performing the same work as them or work of equal value to theirs.

facts.statement: Employers must answer a worker's pay information request within two months at the latest.

citation.quote: Employers shall provide the information referred to in paragraph 1 within a reasonable period of time but in any event within two months from the date on which the request is made.

facts.statement: Employers must inform all workers every year of their right to this pay information and how to use it.

citation.quote: Employers shall inform all workers, on an annual basis, of their right to receive the information referred to in paragraph 1 and of the steps that the worker is to undertake to exercise that right.

facts.statement: Employers with 250 or more workers must report their gender pay gap by 7 June 2027, then every year.

citation.quote: Employers with 250 workers or more shall, by 7 June 2027 and every year thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.

facts.statement: Employers with 150 to 249 workers must report their gender pay gap by 7 June 2027, then every three years.

citation.quote: Employers with 150 to 249 workers shall, by 7 June 2027 and every three years thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.

facts.statement: Employers with 100 to 149 workers must report their gender pay gap by 7 June 2031, then every three years.

citation.quote: Employers with 100 to 149 workers shall, by 7 June 2031 and every three years thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.

facts.statement: Member States can require pay reporting from employers with fewer than 100 workers under national law.

citation.quote: Member States may, as a matter of national law, require employers with fewer than 100 workers to provide information on pay.

facts.statement: Employers can publish their pay gap figures on their website or make them public another way.

citation.quote: The employer may publish the information referred to in paragraph 1, points (a) to (f), of this Article on its website or make it publicly available in another manner.

facts.statement: Pay reporting that shows an average gap of at least 5% in any category of workers triggers a joint pay assessment.

citation.quote: the pay reporting demonstrates a difference in the average pay level between female and male workers of at least 5 % in any category of workers;

facts.statement: The joint pay assessment applies when the employer leaves the unjustified gap unfixed for six months after reporting.

citation.quote: the employer has not remedied such an unjustified difference in the average pay level within six months of the date of submission of the pay reporting.

facts.statement: Member States must give technical help and training to employers with fewer than 250 workers.

citation.quote: Member States shall provide support, in the form of technical assistance and training, to employers with fewer than 250 workers and to the workers’ representatives concerned, to facilitate their compliance with the obligations laid down in this Directive.

facts.statement: Penalties must include fines set under national law, and the text sets no fine amount.

citation.quote: Those penalties shall include fines, the setting of which shall be based on national law.

facts.statement: Compensation for pay discrimination has no upper limit.

citation.quote: The compensation or reparation shall not be restricted by the fixing of a prior upper limit.

facts.statement: An employer that breaches the transparency duties in Articles 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 must prove there was no pay discrimination.

citation.quote: where an employer has not implemented the pay transparency obligations set out in Articles 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10, it is for the employer to prove that there has been no such discrimination.

confidence.reason: The source is the official English text, but French and Spanish transposing laws can add stricter thresholds or earlier dates.
